t: This is a building on Egerton Crescent, in the Kensington and Chelsea part of London. The material I have is thin, so I'll keep to what's known. Daniel Farson, born here in 1927, became a writer and broadcaster. He was prominent in the early days of commercial television, and his sharp, investigative style contrasted with the BBC's more deferential culture. Thomas Stoker, a civil servant of the British Raj, also lived here, and he died here in 1925.
